label: Training loss should decrease at every step
description:
A common belief is that a healthy training run shows the loss falling on every step, and any uptick is a bug. This is wrong for stochastic gradient descent on minibatches: the gradient on one batch is a noisy estimate of the true gradient, so individual steps can and should oscillate. What you want is a downward TREND on a moving average over many steps, not monotonic decrease.

If you actually see monotonic decrease, your batch size is probably enormous (full-batch GD), your learning rate is tiny, or you're plotting a smoothed line and forgetting it's smoothed. Per-step jitter is normal and is part of how SGD escapes shallow saddles.
probeQuestions: If your loss spikes upward on one step but the moving average keeps falling, is training broken?
Why does increasing batch size tend to make per-step loss curves look smoother?
correctionPromptTemplate: The learner thinks loss must drop every step or training is broken. Walk through: SGD's per-batch gradient is a noisy estimator. Per-step jitter is normal; what matters is the trend over hundreds of steps. Ask a calibrated question first — for example, 'why might full-batch GD on a convex problem look smoother than SGD on the same problem?'
